name: Balinese kecak (monkey chant)
lineage: Balinese kecak Indonesian collective-male-chorus a-cappella ritual-and-tourist-performance tradition of the village of Bona (south-central Bali) and surrounding villages, developed in the 1930s by Walter Spies and Wayan Limbak in collaboration with local Balinese performers, drawing on the older sanghyang trance-ceremony chorus tradition. Performance configuration: a circle of 50-150 male performers seated cross-legged, chanting interlocking "chak-chak-chak" rhythmic patterns in characteristic seven-or-more-part hocketed polyrhythm, while a single performer in the center enacts scenes from the Ramayana narrative. The form is one of the most internationally recognized Balinese performance traditions through twentieth-century tourist circuit.
